maya: Heads-up — saw a p95 latency spike on runway-10 (dedicated pool) during the overnight load test. p50 steady but p95 jumped ~270ms -> 630ms around 02:12 UTC.

devin: saw that too. correlates with a bunch of small token requests (avg seq_len ~18) and lots of KV cache misses. Kernel selector fell back to scalar path repeatedly.

sam: any recent rollout that could change kernel heuristics or batch window? :thinking:

olivia: dropping the perf trace — concise snippet:

```
[02:11:49] kernel_select: preferred=vec64 optimistic_ok=false -> fallback_scalar
[02:11:49] batch_assemble: formed 3 microbatches over 110ms
[02:11:49] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.62 prefetch_hit=0.18
[02:11:49] admit: token_credit=1400 -> allow; post_batch_latency=490ms
```

devin: kv miss_rate 0.62 is high. looks like prefetch misalignment + small-batch formation causing bad kernel choice and increased overhead per request. Also token-credit governor allowed too many small requests into the same admit window.

sam: Could be continuous-batching heuristic not seeing enough coalescing due to our admit-window shrinking under load. I remember we lowered default admit-window from 200ms -> 120ms in feb to reduce latency; maybe that interacts badly with small seq_len workloads.

maya: Agreed. Hypothesis: reduced admit-window + aggressive token-credit target causes many tiny batches (<=3) -> kernel chooses scalar fallback -> per-token overhead dominates -> p95 spike.

- disable kv_prefetch for the canary
- bump min_batch_size -> 4
